text: Lesson 16 introduced source and sink connectors abstractly. A concrete source example is change data capture — watching a database's own replication log and turning every change into a Kafka message, in order.
A CDC source connector like Debezium reads the write-ahead log directly, not a polling query — catching every change in the exact order it happened, with no gap and no missed deletes.
On the other end, a sink connector takes messages off a topic and writes them into a destination, like a Snowflake warehouse. Same config shape as the source side, pointed at a different system.
Confluent Cloud's Connectors page, showing a real running connector's status — where you'd monitor whether the CDC source is running and the sink is keeping up.
Chained together, a source and sink connector move data continuously with no custom code written for either hop. That closes out this chapter's start — Kafka Streams and ksqlDB pick up from here.
